summary.text: Michael Bridgford, an independent candidate and Bettendorf-based financial advisor, lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. House in Iowa's 1st District to Christina Bohannan.
He grew up on a family farm near the Quad Cities and holds an MBA from Northwestern University.

paragraphs.text: Bridgford says he grew up on a seventh-generation family farm near the Quad Cities, which is still in the family, and attended public schools with a graduating class of 88. He earned an MBA from Northwestern University.
He says he has worked in financial services, technology, and logistics, previously co-owned a small logistics business, and now works with his father in their financial advisory business.
Bridgford announced his campaign in April 2026 as an independent challenging Republican incumbent Miller-Meeks; Iowa Public Radio described him as the only independent in the race at that time.
He says his campaign collected more than 3,500 petition signatures across all 20 counties in 40 days. He says he lives in Bettendorf with his wife and two daughters.
During the campaign, he emphasized lowering costs and government-reform measures such as term limits and a ban on congressional stock trading.
He received 3.6% of the vote to Christina Bohannan's 53.0%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: Independent candidate enters 'toss up' race for 1st Congressional District
